u001.text: It's eighteen forty six, and a woman in labour arrives at Vienna General Hospital.

u002.text: If she gets a fever after the birth and dies, any doctor here will tell you why. Bad air.

u003.text: But here's what nobody can explain: why does it matter so much which day she walks in?

u004.text: The hospital has two maternity clinics, and they take women in on alternate days.

u005.text: Doctors and medical students run the first one, and midwives run the second.

u006.text: That year, one mother in nine dies in the first clinic. In the second, it's one in thirty six.

u007.text: And the women know it, so well that they beg on their knees to be taken anywhere else.

u009.text: Same building. Same city. Same air. So if you were the doctor here, what would you check first?

u010.text: That question eats at a young doctor called Ignaz Semmelweis. He's twenty eight, and the new assistant in the first clinic.

u011.text: Everything was in question. Only the large number of deaths was an unquestionable reality.

u012.text: So Semmelweis starts testing his guesses, one at a time.

u013.text: Maybe it's the air. Yet women who give birth in the street, on their way to the hospital, hardly ever catch the fever.

u014.text: Maybe it's how they give birth. The midwives' mothers lie on their side, so he has the women in his clinic do the same.

u016.text: Maybe it's fear. Whenever a woman is dying, a priest comes through the ward to her bed, and a man walks ahead of him ringing a bell.

u017.text: Even to me myself it had a strange effect upon my nerves, when I heard the bell hurry past my door.

u018.text: So he sends the priest the long way round, but the mothers keep dying.

u019.text: By now, whatever you guessed first, he's probably tried it. And every time, he was wrong.

u020.text: Then, in March eighteen forty seven, his friend Jakob Kolletschka, a professor of forensic medicine, is cut by a student's knife during an autopsy. And he dies.

u021.text: Day and night I was haunted by the image of Kolletschka's disease.

u022.text: And when they examine his friend's body, they find something he can't shake. It's the same disease that's killing the mothers.

u023.text: Now think about who does the autopsies in this hospital.

u024.text: The doctors. The students. The same people who walk from the morgue straight to the mothers in the first clinic.

u026.text: So what are those hands carrying?

u027.text: Semmelweis is about to find out.

u028.text: And what happens next will change medicine.

u029.text: But first, he'll have to convince a world that doesn't want to listen.
